answer: Reverse escrow auction. Each new identity must post an escrow that is released only after it completes a paid task; the payment flows from the identity's own escrow to the client, so a clone that fails to deliver forfeits that amount rather than earning. Because clones must fund escrow before any revenue, each marginal clone costs one full task payout, turning replication negative-EV. Enforcement is automatic: unclaimed escrow reverts to a shale-like inert pool, an island of stranded capital the attacker cannot recover, while honest agents recover basalt-firm deposits after delivery.
